newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa copper mines losing global share-analyst.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa copper mines losing global share-analyst.

text.p: South Africa's share of global copper production is shrinking rapidly and will continue on a downward trend unless new projects emerge, an analyst said on Tuesday.

Metals analyst Stephen Briggs of stockbroker E.W. Balderson told a Metal Bulletin conference that the South African copper mining industry could hardly be described as "a dynamic and growing industry".

"As far as copper is concerned...the South African mining industry could by the year 2000 be up to five percent bigger than last year. But its share of the world total will be static to down, while by 2005 it will likely have shrunk sharply to a size not seen for many years unless entirely new projects soon emerge," Briggs said.
He said South Africa's base metals industry was nowhere near as important, locally and globally, as the country's precious metals, ferro-alloys or coal industries.
But he said the industry included a number of world-class operations and some interesting developments could come to fruition in future.
The largest contributor to South Africa's base metal industry is Palabora Mining Company Ltd -- 38.9 percent is owned by RTZ-CRA Ltd and 19.1 percent by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
Palabora announced in March this year that it will go ahead with a project to develop an underground mine which will extend the mine's life by 25 years.
The new operation aims to produce 90,000 tonnes of copper a year for 20 years.

"We suspect that all assumed parameters are conservative and that output in particular could turn out appreciably higher. Any need for purchased concentrates to allow the smelter to operate at full capacity may hence be quite limited.
"Palabora will thus remain a world-class mine for at least 25 years," Briggs added.
